name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in frames without bloating compute, giving us a 0.7% quality bump on low-res inputs—critical for aerial footage where blur kills accuracy. Trade-off: it adds a 12% runtime hit, but we offset it by running it only on keyframes, not every frame.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting 12% runtime on a tool that doesn’t address the core problem. Instead, test VFI-Flow’s temporal interpolation first; if it cuts blur by even 0.5%, the trade-off is worth it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by filling gaps in motion paths, directly attacking the core problem of temporal accuracy—where depth-aware upscaling only polishes what’s already there. The trade-off is a 15% runtime increase, but we offset it by running it only on keyframes and letting the lighter depth upscaler handle the rest, keeping the net compute hit under 8%. This delivers the 0.5%+ quality bump we need without wasting effort on spatial fixes that miss the blur.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 15% runtime hit is a gamble—EXCAVA’s temporal bottleneck isn’t blur alone, it’s motion *consistency* across frames. Test it on a 100-frame aerial clip first; if it introduces jitter or ghosting, we’ve wasted compute and time. A safer play: run VFI-Flow *only* on keyframes, then let EXCAVA’s existing temporal smoothing handle the rest—cuts the risk without dropping the ball.
